The behaviour of the receptionist staff is not just rude, but seems to be particularly hostile towards people of colour. After experiencing this myself, I checked the reviews and noticed a pattern—many complaints about the rude and untrained receptionists come overwhelmingly from people of colour, particularly those of Indian/Pakistani descent.

As someone with a severe back injury requiring weekly pain medication, the repeated failures in handling my prescriptions have been incredibly frustrating. On three occasions, I waited two days believing my medication had been ordered, only to be told it hadn’t been. This meant unnecessary trips to the pharmacy, which are particularly difficult for me due to my condition. When I confronted the staff with my call logs proving I had ordered the medication, they bluntly denied it and never once apologized for their mistakes or their embarrassing behaviour.

The issues extend beyond prescriptions. Recently, I called to book an appointment and was given a date and time. However, when I arrived, the receptionist rudely claimed I never made an appointment. Despite showing my call logs as proof, she lied to my face, saying no appointment had been booked. This happened when I had an urgent medical issue. Her response to my distress was a curt, “We are really busy, so do you want another appointment or not?” just after dealing similarly dismissively with another patient.

The lack of accountability is staggering. Today, yet again, they missed my prescription after two days of waiting, with no apologies and the same rude tone insisting it wasn’t ordered.

This surgery needs a serious overhaul of its reception staff and their training. Their behaviour is unacceptable, discriminatory, and has caused unnecessary distress to many patients, including myself. I will be contacting NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde, Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and the Scottish Public Services Ombudsman to file a serious complaint.
